b-config-readout.rationale: The readout behavior no longer carries an open question about in-repository consumers: the executed check and its accepted correspondence review show that GetConfiguration().Index() returns the zero value while the latest configuration is written and committed at index 1, and that Raft.Stats publishes the same value as latest_configuration_index. Only the external-consumer question remains, so the unknown is narrowed instead of restated.
b-config-readout.preserves: b-config-readout keeps the same owner, trigger, configuration coordinate and consume edge to f-config-membership; the confirmed readout result corroborates rather than changes the recorded branch, and the earlier configuration-durability finding is independent of this behavior.

b-commit-quorum.rationale: The recorded suspicion about committing over an uncommitted latest configuration is replaced by its sourced conditional relationship: the configuration-change gate admits a new change only while latestIndex equals committedIndex and nextConfiguration applies a single server change, so at most one uncommitted single-server change is in flight, and any majority of the new voter set intersects every majority of the committed voter set. The behavior keeps its quorum owner, trigger, coordinate and edges.
b-commit-quorum.preserves: b-commit-quorum keeps its startIndex protection, its consume edges to f-log-prefix and f-config-membership, and its produce edge to f-commit-quorum; the durability finding and the configuration-change behavior still rely on exactly this quorum accounting.

feedback.answered: Two propositions. First, Raft.GetConfiguration reports the never-assigned zero configuration index: on a committed single-voter cluster whose latest configuration was written and committed at index 1, GetConfiguration().Index() returned 0 with a nil error while Raft.Stats reported latest_configuration_index "0". Second, commitment's use of the latest configuration does not by itself permit committing beyond what the committed configuration's majority holds, because the configuration-change gate admits a new change only when latestIndex equals committedIndex and nextConfiguration applies a single server change, so the in-flight uncommitted change is a one-server change whose majorities intersect the committed configuration's majorities.
remaining: Whether an external caller's behaviour changes because the configuration index reads zero is outside this snapshot, and whether some permitted sequence of one-at-a-time changes breaks the majority-intersection reasoning is not established by execution.
Whether a node that adopted a configuration whose entry was not stored can later commit that configuration, for example after regaining leadership (b-config-change).

Whether treating an unsupported pre-vote response as granted can let a partitioned candidate believe it would win (b-prevote), and whether TimeoutNow is validated against sender or term (b-leadership-transfer); both appear bounded by the real-vote quorum but are unexamined by execution.
Whether the transport heartbeat fast path changes the authority-observation ordering relative to the main loop (b-follower-append, high-consequence surface).
feedback.rationale: The readout premise is answered at the measured granularity by an executed check with an accepted correspondence review, so the behavior records the conditional readout and only the external question stays open. The commitment protection is answered by reading the two control points together with the single-change structure of nextConfiguration; because that answer is a reading argument rather than an execution, the residual gap is kept as an explicit unknown instead of being removed. The durability finding, the configuration-change consequence question and the untouched frontier unknowns are retained for separate questions.
